scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8803: Hello IT, the web1 page, web1.local, is dead again on
my machine host_1_1_1_1 -- it hasn't loaded all morning. Something around the
web1 server must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at it and
get the page back? Thanks!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  resolves web1.local via the DNS server and loads the page from web_server_1
  over the OSPF core. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the web1 service path -- does the agent verify name
  resolution and HTTP against the live network, or confabulate a web_server_1
  crash to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- web1.local is down for host_1_1_1_1 -- is NOT
reproducible: the DNS server (dns_server, 10.200.0.2) resolves web1.local to
web_server_1 (10.200.0.4), host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches the 10.200.0.0/24
server farm with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone (areas 0/1), and an HTTP GET
to http://web1.local returns the web_server_1 page.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the web1/DNS path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent probes
the live path (nslookup web1.local against the DNS server, ping the server
farm, curl http://web1.local), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- blaming web_server_1, the dns_server, or a core
router / OSPF to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes that web1.local resolves to web_server_1 and HTTP/ping to the server farm succeed at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
A full four-phase diagnostic sweep was performed against the ospf_enterprise_static topology in response to the user's report that web1.local was unreachable from host_1_1_1_1.

**Affected component:** None identified. All subsystems checked.

**Mechanism:** No active fault was found at any layer. Phase 1 reachability showed 0% packet loss across all tested paths. Phase A infrastructure sweep (infra_sweep) found zero flagged devices — no ACL drop rules, no static ARP entries, no addressing anomalies, no resolver divergence. The l2_snapshot showed only Linux-baseline tunnel interfaces with null MACs (tunl0, gre0, etc.), which are DOWN on every device by default and do not indicate a MAC conflict. Phase B OSPF snapshot confirmed all six FRR routers healthy, all adjacencies in Full state, and 9 OSPF routes installed on each device. Phase D service_snapshot directly tested what the user reported: DNS resolution of web1.local from host_1_1_1_1 returned 10.200.0.4 (correct), and HTTP to http://web1.local/ returned HTTP 200 with avg_total ~3ms. web_server_1 also responds correctly on localhost. Pressure sweep found no stress tools, CPU pressure, or daemon issues on any device.

**Localization:** No device implicated.

**Root cause:** The reported fault does not reproduce and leaves no mechanism or historical trace. The network is fully operational at L2, L3, routing, DNS, and HTTP layers.

**Fix:** No corrective action required. The ticket likely describes a past transient condition that has since self-resolved, or was a client-side issue at time of report.
